# The heart at 11 to 14 weeks

> DRAFT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE. Contains claims with status 'ai-extracted' that no clinician has verified.

Unit D9 | Tier: Detect | Version 0.1

## You will be able to

- State the place of early cardiac screening: effective, but not routine or mandatory.
- Give the minimum cardiac check at the early scan.
- List the components of a detailed early cardiac screen.
- Apply the Doppler safety limits for early pregnancy.
- Say which nuchal translucency measurements lead to cardiac referral.

## Where early screening stands

The screening guideline is written for the second trimester. It also considers screening in the late first and early second trimester where this is technically feasible. [1]

First-trimester cardiac screening has been shown to be effective in low-risk populations. It is neither routine nor mandatory. Where possible, it can be done at the nuchal translucency scan. [2]

The cardiac screening examination is performed optimally between 18 and 22 weeks. [3]


## The minimum

The minimum requirements at an early screen are to see the heart within the chest and to confirm a regular rhythm. [4]

Cardiac structures are seen successfully significantly more often after 12 weeks and 3 days. [4]


## Equipment

High-frequency transabdominal transducers are recommended for early screening; a transvaginal transducer may be used. Colour Doppler, high-quality power Doppler, or both are used in addition to grey-scale. [5]

The echocardiography guideline notes that frequencies of 5 to 12 MHz may help in the late first and early second trimesters. [6]


## Safety

In early screening, use Doppler mainly for the four-chamber view and the three-vessel-and-trachea view. Keep the thermal index at 1.0 or less. Keep exposure as short as possible, usually no more than 5 to 10 minutes. [7]

The echocardiography guideline gives the same direction for early gestation: thermal and mechanical indices at or below 1.0, and Doppler used sparingly. [8]


## A detailed early cardiac screen

When a detailed early screen is done, three components are recommended. [9]

| Component | Mode | What to show |
|---|---|---|
| Situs and cardiac axis | Grey-scale | Position and axis of the heart |
| Four-chamber view | Grey-scale, and colour or power Doppler | The four-chamber view on both |
| Three-vessel-and-trachea view | Colour or power Doppler | Aortic and ductal arches, both on the left |


## Limits of the early scan

Outflow-tract views are often difficult in early gestation and are prone to both false-negative and false-positive diagnosis. [10]

Any suspicion at the early scan should lead to referral for early fetal echocardiography. [10]

Some lesions are not discovered until later in pregnancy. [11]

Treat an early look as a first look. See the first item under missing claims: the wording on the later screen is waiting for a source or the editor.


## Nuchal translucency and the heart

A nuchal translucency of 3.5 mm or more at 11 to 14 weeks is an indication for detailed cardiac evaluation. This holds even if the measurement later falls into the normal range. [12]

With a nuchal translucency of 3.0 to 3.4 mm, fetal echocardiography may be considered. [13]

## Early cardiac screen

- [ ] Heart within the chest [4]
- [ ] Rhythm regular [4]
- [ ] Situs and cardiac axis on grey-scale [9]
- [ ] Four-chamber view on grey-scale and on colour or power Doppler [9]
- [ ] Three-vessel-and-trachea view on colour or power Doppler: both arches on the left [9]
- [ ] Thermal index 1.0 or less; Doppler time kept short [7]
- [ ] Nuchal translucency 3.5 mm or more: detailed cardiac evaluation arranged [12]
- [ ] Any suspicion: referred for early fetal echocardiography [10]

## Still to be written (awaiting sourced claims)

- An explicit statement that a normal early cardiac scan does not replace the second-trimester screen - implied by the guideline's scope; needs a direct source or the editor's wording.
- Other first-trimester markers linked to heart disease (tricuspid regurgitation, ductus venosus flow) - not in the screening guideline; needs a source.
- Which lesions can and cannot be detected at 11 to 14 weeks, with detection rates - needs a source.
- Transvaginal technique for the early heart - needs a source.
